/**
 * The Order repository: this entity's key type, its collection, and a factory.
 *
 * The machinery lives in `repository-core` and is shared with every other
 * entity's repository. Adding a second entity means a second file like this
 * one, not a second copy of that.
 */

import { createRepository } from "../lib/core.js";
import type { CollectionSpec, Repository, Store } from "../lib/core.js";

/**
 * The key type for `Order`, distinct from every other kind of key.
 *
 * The brand is what stops `OrderId` and some other entity's id from being
 * interchangeable. They are both strings at runtime, and without this the
 * compiler would accept either wherever the other is expected — which is the
 * mistake that shows up as a lookup that finds nothing for a reason nobody can
 * see.
 */
declare const orderIdBrand: unique symbol;

export type OrderId = string & { readonly [orderIdBrand]: true };

/**
 * The only constructor for `OrderId`, so every key in the program has been
 * through this check.
 *
 * @throws TypeError when the value is empty or padded, since a key that differs
 * from another only by whitespace is a bug waiting for a support ticket.
 */
export function orderId(value: string): OrderId {
  if (value === "" || value.trim() !== value) {
    throw new TypeError(
      "OrderId must be a non-empty string with no surrounding whitespace.",
    );
  }
  return value as OrderId;
}

/**
 * The minimum `Order` must have to be stored: its key.
 *
 * Your own `Order` satisfies this by having an `id`, so nothing here needs to
 * know the rest of its fields. That is deliberate — a generated file that
 * declared your domain type would have to be edited every time the domain
 * changed, and regenerating it would then overwrite the edit.
 */
export interface OrderRecord {
  readonly id: OrderId;
}

/**
 * Where Order records live, and how one yields its key.
 *
 * Exported so that a datastore adapter can be told which collections exist
 * without importing every entity's factory.
 */
export const ORDERS: CollectionSpec<OrderRecord, OrderId> = {
  collection: "orders",
  keyField: "id",
  key: (record) => record.id,
};

/**
 * A repository over orders, typed to your own `Order`.
 *
 * Pass your domain type: `createOrderRepository<Order>(store)`. The constraint
 * is only that it has an `id`, so every method is typed in terms of your type
 * rather than ours.
 */
export function createOrderRepository<T extends OrderRecord>(
  store: Store,
): Repository<T, OrderId> {
  return createRepository<T, OrderId>(store, {
    collection: ORDERS.collection,
    keyField: "id",
    key: (record) => record.id,
  });
}
